paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the LORD is in charge of every nation and every power, and that includes the ones that look unbeatable. Egypt had a Pharaoh, a mighty army, hired soldiers and its own gods. And the LORD says He is the One who thrust the warriors down (Jeremiah 46:15) and will punish Amon, Pharaoh and "those who trust in Pharaoh" (Jeremiah 46:25). So the question for you and me is simple: who are we trusting?

Look at how the warriors describe that Pharaoh: "all noise" (Jeremiah 46:17). Friend, I have been all noise in my own bakery, and the cookies did not care. The LORD also names "those who trust in Pharaoh" among the ones He is about to punish (Jeremiah 46:25). So it's worth asking what we're leaning on, and whether there's anything behind it.

Now hear the other half, because the LORD does. To His servant Jacob He says, "do not be afraid, and do not be dismayed" (Jeremiah 46:27), and then He says it again: "do not be afraid, declares the LORD, for I am with you" (Jeremiah 46:28). He promises to save Jacob's descendants from the land of their captivity, and He is honest that He will "discipline you justly" too (Jeremiah 46:27-28). Those words were spoken to Jacob, but they show us the LORD's heart for His people: fear doesn't get the last word, because He is with them.
